data.name: Renegade Grounds: Episode 1
data.detailed_description:
Synopsis:

Something very important was stolen from the council – a high value item required for a new device that could bridge the gap between the physical realm and the realm of phantoms. Who did this and why is unknown, but the city guard hired two mercenaries to find and retrieve this item in return for a hefty sum – Agela, a young, somewhat brash, and quick-witted archer, and her smarty pants imp sidekick Ingus.

Agela and Ingus will have to infiltrate their way into crime-ridden slums, as well as a whole host of underground and treacherous locations in order to get the job done. On their journey they are guided by a phantom ally, Angadani, who appears from time to time to update them with useful information. A simple fetch job quickly becomes more complex as more factions become involved and set their eyes on the precious item. It's more than they bargained for, but to Agela and Ingus, giving up is not an option!

Features:
  • Not your typical fantasy setting. Medieval look and non-human races, but more with a modern day dynamic – gangs, crime-infested slums, city councils instead of kings in castles, and science instead of magic.
  • Strategic turn-based battle system which includes skills with unique areas of effect.
  • Fully voice acted
  • Weapon and Armour upgrading – find specific items which can be used to add a variety of stat bonuses to your equipment, but do so wisely, because each weapon and armour has a limited number of upgrade slots.
  • First part of a larger story
  • In addition to story mode, challenge yourself with consecutive battles in arena mode
  • Two difficulty modes: Normal and Brazen
  • Puzzles to solve and secret areas to find!

If you want to support this game and all my other past and future games further, please check out my patreon page below!

data.short_description: First episode of a thrilling adventure! Two mercenaries, Agela and Ingus, are tasked to infiltrate the criminal underworld to retrieve a device of high value that was stolen from the council. The job gets more complex as more factions join the hunt for the item, but to Agela and Ingus, failure is not an option!

reviews.review:
Renegade Grounds: Episode 1 is a modest indie role-playing game that tries to give the familiar 2D fantasy RPG formula a less conventional identity. Developed by Astronomic Games and published by New Reality Games, it combines turn-based battles, exploration, equipment improvement, environmental puzzles, secrets, an arena mode, and a narrative built around mercenaries, criminals, science, and supernatural beings. Its RPG Maker heritage is immediately apparent in the presentation, but the game compensates for its technical simplicity by attempting to establish a setting that does not completely depend on the usual fantasy stereotypes.

The adventure follows Agela and Ingus, a pair of mercenaries hired by the city guard after an important object is stolen from the council. This is more than an ordinary piece of valuable property because it is associated with research into a device capable of connecting the physical world with the realm inhabited by phantoms. With little information concerning the thief or the reasons behind the robbery, the protagonists begin what appears to be a relatively straightforward recovery mission. Their investigation soon draws them into a wider struggle as other factions reveal their own interest in the stolen object.

Agela and Ingus provide much of the personality behind the story. Agela is an outspoken archer whose confidence and impulsiveness contrast with the more intellectually inclined Ingus, an imp who accompanies her throughout the mission. Their exchanges help prevent the adventure from becoming excessively serious, while the phantom Angadani provides additional guidance and information. Full English voice acting is a notable inclusion for a production of this scale. Although the performances and overall presentation naturally lack the polish of a large commercial RPG, hearing the characters speak gives conversations additional character and helps distinguish the principal cast.

The world is arguably more interesting than the basic visual presentation initially suggests. Instead of concentrating entirely on monarchies, knights, wizards, and traditional magical institutions, the setting incorporates municipal authorities, mercenary employment, organized crime, dangerous urban districts, scientific experimentation, and supernatural phenomena. Science effectively occupies some of the narrative territory normally reserved for conventional magic. The result is still recognizably fantasy, but the social structure and central conflict give it a slightly different flavor.

Exploration takes the party through troubled city districts and increasingly dangerous underground locations, including caves, mines, tunnels, and related environments. Hidden locations reward players willing to investigate beyond the obvious route, while puzzles interrupt the regular cycle of movement and combat. These elements are not elaborate enough to transform the game into a dedicated puzzle adventure, but they provide welcome changes of pace and make exploration somewhat more meaningful than simply moving between enemy encounters.

Combat uses a turn-based system with abilities that can affect different areas and groups of targets. This introduces a useful tactical consideration because the best action depends on the composition of the opposing group rather than merely selecting the most damaging attack available. The mechanics remain approachable and comparatively simple, making the game easy to understand for players familiar with traditional indie RPGs. Normal and Brazen difficulty choices provide some flexibility, with the latter better suited to players who want encounters to demand more careful decisions.

Character development is supported by an equipment upgrade system. Weapons and armor can receive statistical improvements through upgrade items found during the adventure, but each piece of equipment has a limited number of available upgrade slots. Consequently, deciding which improvements to install carries more importance than it would in a system where equipment can be enhanced indefinitely. It is not an exceptionally deep customization model, yet it gives exploration and resource acquisition additional value while allowing players to shape their equipment according to their preferred approach.

Players interested primarily in combat can also spend time in an arena that presents consecutive encounters. This gives the battle mechanics an additional purpose beyond story progression and provides opportunities to test character development against repeated opposition. The presence of numerous achievements adds another incentive for completion-oriented players to investigate optional content and engage with the different systems.

The game's largest limitations come from its scale and presentation. The visuals are functional rather than impressive, and anyone expecting elaborate animation, detailed environments, or the production standards of a modern mainstream RPG will need to adjust expectations considerably. Much of its value instead comes from the unusual setting, character interactions, straightforward combat, and exploration. The episodic format is another consideration because this first installment functions as the beginning of a broader storyline rather than a massive standalone adventure with every narrative thread comprehensively resolved.

Steam Deck compatibility should be treated cautiously. The game does not have an official Steam Deck Verified or Playable rating. Its relatively undemanding 2D presentation and controller support suggest that it has characteristics suitable for portable play, but those qualities should not be mistaken for guaranteed compatibility. Steam Deck users may encounter situations requiring compatibility settings or manual adjustments, so its status is best described as officially unverified.

Renegade Grounds: Episode 1 ultimately works best for players who appreciate small independent RPGs and can overlook dated or inexpensive presentation when the underlying ideas are interesting. Its combination of turn-based encounters, area-based abilities, limited equipment upgrades, secrets, puzzles, arena battles, voice acting, and an unusual science-meets-fantasy setting gives the experience more personality than its simple exterior might indicate. The episodic structure and limited production values prevent it from becoming an essential RPG, but there is enough ambition here to make it an intriguing curiosity for dedicated fans of traditional 2D role-playing adventures.

Rating: 5/10
